preamble: Depalatalization of [ʃ] to [s] involves the movement of the articulation from the post-alveolar to the alveolar region. In Samic, Proto-Uralic *š merged completely with *s (*iša 'skin' > Proto-Samic *ësē), while Finnic took the opposite route to h.

examples.note: While most [ʃ] became [x] in Modern Spanish, in some dialects and loanwords, it shifted to [s].
Greek lacks [ʃ] and often adapts this sound from loanwords as [s].
The palatal sibilant became Lithuanian š but Latvian s

examples.to: Proto-Samic *ësē > Northern Sami assi 'scalp', Skolt Sami ââʹss
examples.note: Reconstructed stage: Proto-Uralic *š merged with *s in Proto-Samic, whereas Finnic turned it into h (Finnish iho 'skin').

examples.to: Proto-Samic *pësē > Northern Sami bassi, Lule Sami basse
examples.note: Reconstructed stage; contrast Finnish pyhä 'holy' with h from the same *š.

examples.to: Proto-Samic *posōtēk > Northern Sami bossut, Inari Sami possoođ
examples.note: Reconstructed stage; contrast Proto-Finnic *puhudak (Finnish puhua) with h.
